Posit Assistant asks for confirmation on every file it edits. Turning that off
wholesale gives an assistant that will also push to a shared branch and send a
data frame to a model provider. The setting that sits between the two is
`approvalMode`, and the file it belongs in is `.posit/assistant/settings.json`
in the project root, committed so that everyone working in the repository gets
the same posture.

The recommended file is two settings long, and the specification says why it
is that short. The test is whether git can undo the thing a rule would prevent,
which removes almost every rule anyone would think to write. The specification
also compares the `auto` and `normal` modes, carries a checklist of behaviors
with a verdict on each, and records what the assistant sends to a provider
without being asked. The last of those is the finding to read first if the
project holds patient data.

No behavior in it has been observed in Positron yet. Eight open questions
remain, three of which take about ten minutes each.

## Documents

- [Working specification](specification.qmd). The recommended settings file,
  the test that keeps it short, `auto` against `normal`, the checklist of
  behaviors, the sandbox, the limits of what any settings file enforces, and
  the open questions.
- [References](references.qmd). The Posit documentation, the general
  cross-vendor guidance on agent permissions, and a marker on each recording
  whether the claim drawn from it has been checked against the source.
